entities.summary: Drusus Julius Caesar, also called Drusus the Younger, was the son of Emperor Tiberius, and heir to the Roman Empire following the death of his adoptive brother Germanicus in AD 19. He played a pivotal role in the Roman Empire's reorganization and expansion under the guidance of his father. Drusus Julius Caesar was appointed as the governor of Germania Superior, and his military campaigns helped to establish Roman control over the region. His efforts to integrate Germanic tribes into the Roman Empire laid the groundwork for future expansion. Drusus Julius Caesar's legacy is also seen in the establishment of the Roman province of Germania Inferior, which he founded during his reign. He died suddenly in 23 CE at the age of 42, leaving behind a vast empire that would continue to shape the course of European history. As the Roman historian Tacitus wrote, 'Drusus was a man of great energy and courage, and the father of the emperor Augustus.' Drusus Julius Caesar's untimely death was a significant event in Roman history, and his impact on the empire's future was felt for centuries to come.
